description: View the NYC skyline from across the Hudson River in New Jersey, looking east. Tests whether the skill guides positioning camera AWAY from the target for a panoramic cityscape view.
name: archive-nyc-skyline-from-hudson
notes: Imported from optimization/scenarios/cesiumjs-camera/eval-005. Expected source/runtime contracts are scenario-authored; actual values are observed from the archived baseline generated JS and browser artifacts.

expected_behaviors: Camera positioned west of Manhattan (longitude more negative than -74.0)
Pitch near horizontal or slightly down (-5 to -15 degrees)
Uses flyTo or setView (not lookAt — this is a positioned view, not an orbital lock)
Adds a visible Manhattan skyline proxy made from vertical geometry
preflight.visual_expectations: The Manhattan skyline viewed from the west across the Hudson River. The waterfront and piers should be visible, with a row of vertical skyline proxy bars over Manhattan so the visual subject reads as a recognizable skyline rather than a flat basemap. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.

prompt: Position the camera in the air over the Hudson River, west of Manhattan, looking east toward the NYC skyline. I want to see the full Manhattan skyline as if photographing it from across the river at about 500 meters altitude. Camera should be roughly at coordinates 40.7484 N, 74.02 W (over the Hudson), looking east. Because public OSM imagery can render this as a flat map with no skyline, add a simplified skyline proxy along Manhattan: multiple vertical colored boxes or cylinders of different heights at recognizable Midtown/Downtown waterfront positions, including a taller Empire State Building marker. The skyline bars should be visible across the river and should read as a city skyline, not as tiny points.
